answer: Because the cipher index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the voyage audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 136 answers need 136 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the nebula identifier and voids the later submissions, which means the operator burns for 136 runs and collects one. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
